To make sure your contact lens prescription is accurate, we’ll have a board-certified ophthalmologist review your exam results. Your new prescription will be valid everywhere, so, basically, renewing your contacts prescription online is the future. And it’s glorious.
The oh-so-satisfying answer is that it depends. On what? Primarily your age and eye health. See what the American Academy of Ophthalmology says about how often you should visit the eye doctor.

Folks get eye exams for lots of reasons: health concerns, to get or renew a prescription for vision correction, etc. so the length of exam can vary. We have some info that may help you estimate the length of your visit.

Telemedicine isn't just for your traditional family doctor. You can now renew your prescription online to skip the long and expensive trip to the eye doctor. Here are the differences between a traditional eye exam and what's offered online.
Read more
An online vision exam is a convenient and affordable way to renew your contact lens or glasses prescription from home. No appointments necessary.
While an average, in-office comprehensive eye exam elsewhere costs $150 on average, our “just-renew-my-prescription” online eye exam is just $20. That’s worth a surprise double-take.

A comprehensive eye exam at your eye doctor usually takes an hour plus driving time. Our online vision exam takes only 10 minutes to complete, and you can expect results usually around two business hours. (And no driving required.)

Taking an online eye exam is easy. All you need is your laptop and ten feet of space. Click any button above to get started. We’ll walk you through your eye exam, which should take only about 10 minutes to complete.

It’s usually a good idea to get a comprehensive eye exam every one to two years, depending on your overall health. But if you want to change contact brands or renew an expired prescription without another trip to the eye doctor, you may be able to take a vision exam online.

Vision insurance usually covers one regular, in-network visit with your eye care provider per year (costs $150 on average). You may need to pay an additional copay depending on your insurance plan. Many insurance providers also cover the cost of an online vision exam. (And if not, ours is only $20.)
Currently, our ExpressExam costs $20. The total cost of most standard, comprehensive online eye exams with fitting is $150 ($100 for the exam and $50 for the fitting) on average.

Online eye exams are available in Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Washington D.C., Wisconsin, and Wyoming.

Currently, you cannot use ExpressExam as your online eye exam in Delaware, Hawaii, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, New Jersey, New Mexico, South Carolina, South Dakota, West Virginia, or the U.S. Territories.
